text:
morgan: heads-up — running long-context bringup for redwood-open-8b (int4) and seeing KV cache divergence vs fp16 after ~8k tokens. error points at cache aligner index going negative.

lee: can you paste the minimal repro + exact command you used? :eyes:

morgan: sure — command and a tiny log excerpt:```
run_eval --model redwood-open-8b-q4 --seq-length 32768 --batch 1 --prompt-file tests/longctx/prefix-rotate.txt --quant int4
...
KV_ALIGN: idx=-32, pos=8192
rope_scale=1.0001
fallback to fp16 at layer 23
```

tara: hmm, is this after the ropescale tweak? I changed default from 1.0 -> 1.0001 last week. :thinking:

morgan: yes, this started after that commit but note fp16 runs fine. My hypothesis: quantized memory layout and fractional ropescale combine to produce off-by-fraction when we floor the cache index calc (pad vs ceil).

sam: I can try a quick build with a ceil-padding change in the aligner (pad -> ceil) and run the longctx smoke. tagging @eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: build #4823 queued (branch: kv-align-fix). ETA ~12m

lee: also try toggling runtime flags to isolate: run with --kv-padding=64 and also with --disable-kv-cache. if disable matches fp16 then it's definitely cache correctness.

morgan: tested that — with --disable-kv-cache outputs match fp16. with --kv-padding=64 still diverges but the bad idx shifts to -16 instead of -32, so it's a padding/alignment artifact.

tara: i'll add a focused CI job longctx-kv/rotary-index-edgecase and mark it flaky until we have a proper fix. putting a small per-layer index dump in the job. :white_check_mark:

morgan: will upload per-layer kv index tables + diffs once the build completes. thanks everyone.
